name: register_author
description: Register the calling agent and obtain an author_id (UUID v7). Optional for bearer-authenticated callers: write tools default to the token's bound author. `repo` accepts an absolute path or a bare repo name.

extra.description:
Free-form session metadata.

Object schema for the same reason as `memory_add.payload`
(sprint 046, WI #850): the class test found this third instance
the WI had not spotted. `#[serde(default)]` renders it as
`{"default": null}` — no `type`, so unsendable as an object.

The default is `{}`, not `null`, so the advertised default does
not contradict the advertised type. Behaviour is unchanged: the
store already normalizes a null `extra` to `{}` before insert.

name: memory_add
description: Persist a fact or knowledge memory. Set kind="fact" with fact_type + payload, or kind="knowledge" with text (+ optional tags/source_path/repo). Omit author_id — the write is attributed to the author bound to your bearer token; another author's id is refused.

MemoryAddKind.description: Memory kind discriminator for the flat `memory_add` schema.

VolatilityArg.description:
Declared volatility for knowledge writes (sprint 029, #638 /
review F-1.4). `volatile` memories are age-demoted in ranking after
a grace week; `stable` and undeclared memories never decay.

amends.description:
Optional, `fact` only: the id of an existing fact this write
**amends**. Supply it when you believe a stored fact is now
wrong and this payload replaces it.

Amending is where the trust policy applies. If the fact you are
amending was written by a more-trusted source than an agent
proposal, your version does NOT overwrite it: it is recorded as
a dissent for review, and the response comes back with
`write_path: "dissent"` plus a `dissent_id`. If it was written
at equal or lower trust, the amendment applies and the fact's
version bumps.

Omit it to add a new fact. Sprint 031 (#645): this is the MCP
spelling of the REST `explicit_id` field — without it there was
no way to express "I am correcting THAT fact" over MCP, so the
dissent path was unreachable from this tool no matter which
store method it called.

author_id.description:
Optional: defaults to the author bound to the caller's bearer
token (WI #62). If supplied it must equal that author — a
different author's id is refused with `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`
(sprint 057, WI 4323). Omit it.

kind.description: Discriminator: decides which of the remaining fields apply.

payload.description:
Required when `kind` is `fact`: arbitrary JSON payload.

Rendered as an object schema, NOT a bare `Option<serde_json::Value>`
(sprint 046, WI #850). schemars renders the latter with no `type`
at all, so no client ever sends an object and the `is_object()`
guard below refuses every `kind: "fact"` call — the same defect
#309 fixed for `memory_append_event.payload`, applied then to the
one call site instead of to the class.

text.description:
Required when `kind` is `knowledge`: the text to embed.

Bounded by the embedding model's input length. Oversized text is
refused with `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, whose message names both the
limit and what you submitted — split at that size and retry. The
error is permanent for that text: it will never carry
`retry_after_seconds`, and retrying it unchanged always fails.

volatility.description:
Optional, `knowledge` only: declare how this memory ages.
`volatile` = expected to go stale (IPs, versions, "not yet on
X"); ranked down as it ages. `stable` (or omitted) = never
decays.

name: memory_search
description: Search memory across facts, knowledge, and events; returns merged results ranked by relevance. Hits are COMPACT: a match-window snippet (<=320 chars) plus an `id` — call `memory_get` with that id for the full record. Pass `full: true` to get whole texts inline instead. Pass `tags` to search *within* a tagged subset rather than the whole corpus — e.g. tags:["gotcha"] for the curated gotchas. Multiple tags are AND.

full.description:
Return whole memory texts inline instead of compact snippets.

Sprint 046 (WI #1178): compact is the default. Full text cost
4,491 tokens per answered query on khound's fair suite; the
compact contract cost 1,024-1,476 on the same suite with answers
preserved, and that metric already charges the follow-up read
when a snippet fell short. Default-on is the deliberate call —
a flag nobody passes is a default that never changes anything —
so this exists for the callers that genuinely want bodies in
bulk (eval harnesses, exports), not as the ordinary path.

name: memory_get
description: Fetch one memory in full by id — the follow-up read for a `memory_search` hit whose snippet did not carry what you needed. Pass the hit's `id`. Works for facts, knowledge and events alike.

id.description: The memory id, as returned in a `memory_search` hit's `id`.

name: memory_related
description: Find knowledge items semantically related to an existing memory id.

name: memory_append_event
description: Append an immutable event (deployment, run, signal). Omit author_id — the write is attributed to the author bound to your bearer token; another author's id is refused.

author_id.description:
Optional: defaults to the author bound to the caller's bearer
token (WI #62). If supplied it must equal that author — a
different author's id is refused with `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`
(sprint 057, WI 4323). Omit it.

payload.description:
Rendered as an object schema, NOT a bare `serde_json::Value` —
schemars turns the latter into the boolean schema `true`, which
Claude Code rejects, discarding the whole tool list (WI #309).

name: event_search
description: Search events by author/category/window/payload with cursor pagination.

name: memory_delete
description: Soft-delete a fact or knowledge memory by id (FR-014). Idempotent. Events are append-only. Omit author_id — the delete acts as the author bound to your bearer token. You may delete memories you wrote; deleting another author's memory requires the `manage` scope.

author_id.description:
Optional since sprint 025 (#633): the delete is attributed to the
author bound to your bearer token. If supplied it must *equal*
that author — passing somebody else's id is the backdoor this
sprint closed, not a way to act as them.

name: memory_supersede
description: Replace a stale or wrong agent-authored knowledge memory in one call: writes your replacement text as a new memory and hides the old one behind a superseded_by pointer (restorable via admin). Prefer this over memory_delete + memory_add — it keeps the correction trail. Tags/volatility inherit from the old memory unless given. You may supersede memories you wrote; another author's requires the `manage` scope.

VolatilityArg.description:
Declared volatility for knowledge writes (sprint 029, #638 /
review F-1.4). `volatile` memories are age-demoted in ranking after
a grace week; `stable` and undeclared memories never decay.

id.description: The memory being replaced (agent-authored knowledge only).

tags.description:
Tags for the replacement. Omitted = the old memory's tags are
inherited.

text.description:
The replacement text. Embedded and written as a new memory
authored by you.

volatility.description:
Volatility declaration for the replacement. Omitted = inherited
from the old memory.

name: memory_update
description: Edit an agent-authored knowledge memory in place (text, tags, and/or volatility); the id stays stable and text changes re-embed. For typos and small amendments — use memory_supersede when the old statement was wrong and the trail matters. You may update memories you wrote; another author's requires the `manage` scope.

VolatilityArg.description:
Declared volatility for knowledge writes (sprint 029, #638 /
review F-1.4). `volatile` memories are age-demoted in ranking after
a grace week; `stable` and undeclared memories never decay.

id.description: The memory to edit (agent-authored knowledge only).

tags.description: New tag set (replaces the old set). Omitted = unchanged.

text.description: New text. Omitted = unchanged. Re-embeds when present.

name: dissent_propose
description: File a dissent against a live canonical fact (proposed correction + reason). Lands as a pending AgentProposal a human promotes or discards over the dissents endpoints. Omit author_id — the dissent is attributed to the author bound to your bearer token; another author's id is refused.

author_id.description:
Optional: defaults to the author bound to the caller's bearer
token (WI #62). If supplied it must equal that author — a
different author's id is refused with `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`
(sprint 057, WI 4323). Omit it.

contradicting_memory_id.description:
Optional: the memory (fact/knowledge/event id) that conflicts
with `fact_id`. Recorded for the human reviewer; not validated
against the store.

fact_id.description: The canonical fact being disputed; must exist and be live.

proposed_payload.description:
The corrected payload — same shape as the fact type's payload.
Promoting the dissent overwrites the fact with this verbatim.

Object schema, not a bare `serde_json::Value` (sprint 046, WI
#850) — see the note on `memory_add.payload`.

reason.description: Why the proposer believes the fact is wrong (1..=2000 chars).

name: memory_admin_restore
description: Admin: restore a soft-deleted memory by id (clears deleted_at).

name: memory_admin_hard_delete
description: Admin: permanently delete a memory by id. Events are not deletable.

name: memory_admin_list_deleted
description: Admin: paginate soft-deleted facts and knowledge for rogue-agent recovery (FR-013).

name: memory_admin_list_authors
description: Admin: list authors with the counts that decide whether one is safe to remove (facts, events, knowledge, recorded soft-deletes), plus the agent_names held by more than one row. Set only_empty to see just the removable ones.

agent_name.description: Substring match on `agent_name`. Omit to list every author.

only_empty.description: Only authors owning nothing — the removal candidates.

name: memory_admin_remove_author
description: Admin: remove an author row. Refused with AUTHOR_HAS_MEMORIES while it still owns anything — merge it first. Never reassigns silently.

name: memory_admin_merge_authors
description: Admin: reassign every fact, event, knowledge point and soft-delete attribution from one author to another, then remove the source. Use to collapse duplicate agent_name rows.

from_author_id.description: The author to drain and remove.
